data.name: Harshvardhan
data.gender_notes: Harshvardhan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: God's Harshest, Cruelest, or Most Valiant
data.long_meaning: The name Harshvardhan is derived from two Sanskrit words: Harsh (harsham) and Vardhan (vardhayati). Harsh means 'harsh, cruel, or severe,' while Vardhan means 'nourisher, sustainer, or one who strengthens.' In Hindu mythology, the name Harshvardhan is associated with Lord Vishnu, who is known to have both harsh and merciful aspects. He is believed to be the sustainer of the universe and the provider of spiritual nourishment.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of God's immense power and compassion, embodying both harshness and kindness.
data.etymology: Harshvardhan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's Harshest, Cruelest, or Most Valiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Harshvardhan total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

It highlights the paradoxical nature of the divine, who can be fierce yet loving, harsh yet sustaining. In Indian culture, this name is often given to children, especially boys, to remind them of the duality of life.
data.spiritual_significance: Harshvardhan represents the idea that even in harshness, there resides the power to nourish and sustain. The name symbolizes the transformative power of the divine and the idea that even difficult circumstances can be sources of strength and growth.
